title: Vermillion Platform - Private Networking Intake
summary: Discovery focused on private/VPC deployment options. Customer will evaluate Private (VPC) deployment vs Dedicated; key concerns: egress and region restrictions, transit gateway vs peering, BYOK/KMS, audit logs for SOC2, network IP planning. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share network checklist, draft IP plan template, security whitepaper and pilot pricing; customer to provide VPC CIDR, peering contacts, and desired region list by next week.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-15 15:00 UTC - Duration approx 48 mins. Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Lin (Redwood SE), Alex Rios (Vermillion CTO), Priya Nair (Lead Cloud Eng), Omar Haddad (Security), Lisa Chen (Network).

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intros, i run the enterprise motion here at Redwood. maya handles the infra and private deployments.
[00:15] Maya: hi all, hi alex, priya, omar, lisa. we'll try to cover network, security, and what a pilot looks like. feel free to interrupt.
[00:30] Alex: thanks, we are exploring options to host inference for our customer-facing features. main questions are about private networking, region restrictions, and our compliance needs — SOC2 and some in-country controls.
[00:45] Jordan: great. can you share a bit of context on current infra and traffic patterns?
[00:55] Priya: sure. vermillion runs primarily in us-east-1 and europe-west-1. we have a hybrid app — most traffic goes through our api gateway in us-east. we plan to keep tokens and PII in-region, so data residency matters. at peak we do about 2k requests per minute to our NLU endpoints, but inference calls are smaller subset ~150-300 rpm initially.
[01:25] Lisa: we also have strict egress rules. anything leaving our vpc must go through our corporate firewall/VPN and be logged. we prefer private endpoints, not NAT’ed public egress.
[01:40] Maya: makes sense. Redwood Private supports VPC peering and private endpoints (we call them private egress endpoints internally). depending on cloud provider, we also support transit gateway setups. there are tradeoffs — can i walk through them quickly?
[01:55] Alex: please.
[02:00] Maya: ok so option A is VPC peering: simple, low-latency, but mesh complexity increases with N peers. best for small number of vpcs. option B is Transit Gateway or cloud equivalent: scales better for many vpcs, centralizes routing, and simplifies egress policies. option C is PrivateLink / Private Endpoints: you create aws privatelink endpoints into our service — this gives stable private IPs and avoids NAT, but sometimes more setup on the infra side.
[02:35] Priya: we're leaning away from NAT. private endpoints look good. question: can we force traffic through our egress fw? sometimes privatelink bypasses firewall appliances.
[02:45] Maya: good callout. if you need egress inspection we normally route traffic into your transit gateway where it can be forced through your firewall. with privatelink you can combine endpoints and a transit path so inspection still happens, but it's config heavy.
[03:05] Omar: for SOC2 audit we need full request logs and proof of key management. does Redwood store keys? what's BYOK?
[03:14] Jordan: we support BYOK — you can bring your KMS keys and we integrate with customer-managed KMS in Private deployments. we also have an HSM option for enterprise. audit logs are available per request with token-level metadata in the console, and we can provide log-forwarding to your SIEM.
[03:35] Omar: great. do those logs include request payloads? we typically only want metadata and hashes for PII reasons.
[03:42] Maya: by default we log metadata and non-sensitive fields; payload logging can be disabled or hashed. for SOC2 we provide audit trails, admin activity logs, and enrollment documentation.
[03:55] Lisa: ip planning — what do you need from us?
[04:00] Maya: typical ask is a /24 for the private endpoints, and peering ranges that don't overlap with our service range. we also need a bouncing IP range if you plan to use egress NAT for outbound callbacks. we can share an IP planning template.
[04:14] Priya: okay share template. also region gating — can we restrict which regions our data can be served from? we can't have model inference run in ap-southeast-1 for some customers.
[04:25] Jordan: yes, Private supports region allow-lists. you can pin models and traffic to specific regions. for Hosted customers we have region controls too but Private gives you full control.
[04:40] Alex: latency targets — for our chat experiences we need p95 < 250ms ideally. for longer prompts it's fine to be higher. what's realistic on your side?
[04:52] Maya: on a Private deployment inside the same region and with local NVMe-backed inference nodes, p95 for single-turn short prompts often lands around 80-180ms depending on model size and sequence length. Dedicated reserved pools with optimized kernels can push that lower. our tradeoff is typically latency vs cost — quantization and smaller model variants reduce cost but can change quality.
[05:15] Priya: do you have recommended batch sizes to hit throughput targets? we worry about spiky traffic.
[05:21] Maya: yes, Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and autoscaling profiles. for spiky workloads we recommend a small warm pool and burst capacity; policy-based routing will fallback to lower-cost variants when you exceed capacity.
[05:36] Lisa: network egress bandwidth — if we onboard many tenants simultaneously will bandwidth be a problem? we have 1Gbps between regions and need to understand token throughput.
[05:46] Maya: we usually size for token bandwidth and batching. for text generation the bandwidth per request is small unless you stream many tokens. we'll include guidance in the network checklist.
[05:58] Alex: any limitations on private deployment on prem? we have one datacenter with strict airgap for selected customers.
[06:06] Jordan: Redwood Private has an on-prem package. air-gapped installs are possible but require separate scoping and longer timelines for cert validation and support. most customers start in cloud-VPC and then move to on-prem for specific workloads.
[06:22] Omar: encryption in flight and at rest? we need TLS mutual auth for endpoints.
[06:27] Maya: mutual TLS is supported for service-to-service. at rest we use customer-managed KMS or disk encryption depending on deployment. logs can be forwarded encrypted to your SIEM.
[06:40] Alex: ok good. what's a typical pilot plan?
[06:44] Jordan: typical pilot is 4-6 weeks: initial network setup, private endpoints/peering, a small capacity footprint for load testing (10-50 rps), and a runbook for fallback to hosted endpoints if needed. we'll provide a benchmark harness.
[07:00] Priya: about failover — if the private region goes down do you have automatic fallback? can we force fallback to a specific region?
[07:07] Maya: we support policy-based routing. you can configure a preferred region list and fallback targets. if strict residency is required you can disable fallback. otherwise we recommend a fallback for availability.
[07:22] Lisa: do you support AWS RAM or resource sharing? we use AWS Organizations heavily.
[07:27] Maya: yes we can integrate with org-level resource sharing for endpoints; details vary by cloud. we'll surface the exact instructions in the checklist.
[07:38] Jordan: quick note — sometimes transcripts from earlier calls mention product names like "Redwood Privy" in our internal notes, disregard — that's a transcription artifact.
[07:48] Alex: ha, noted.
[07:52] Omar: security review — would you provide SOC2 artifact access and an architecture diagram for our auditors?
[07:59] Jordan: yes, we can provide SOC2 report and a redactable architecture diagram and compliance pack. for deep audits we do an in-person or scheduled architectural review with our security team.
[08:12] Priya: we also need to know how upgrades and model rollouts are handled — don't want silent regressions.
[08:18] Maya: Redwood supports pinned model versions and canary rollouts. you can pin your traffic to a specific model sha and do canary percentages with automatic rollback based on perf/quality metrics. we also have evaluation hooks for prompt sets.
[08:35] Alex: good. pricing: what's the delta between Dedicated and Private?
[08:40] Jordan: Private includes the platform and private control plane; pricing depends on footprint and support tier. Dedicated is reserved hardware in Redwood-managed infra; Private (VPC) has additional setup and support costs. we'll share a draft pricing sheet.
[08:58] Priya: for network specifics we need: your service ip ranges, endpoint cidr suggestions, peering requirements, port lists, and expected source ports.
[09:09] Maya: agreed — we'll provide a network checklist and an ip plan template.
[09:14] Lisa: what about route table updates — do you require us to add routes for every node?
[09:18] Maya: with privatelink you just create NLB endpoint and accept the endpoint service; for peering we will provide a minimal set of route updates. transit gateway most of the work is on your side but it's simpler at scale.
[09:33] Alex: two quick red flags from our infra lead: 1) we can't expose any admin UI to the public internet, 2) need RBAC and SSO integration.
[09:42] Jordan: for the admin console we can deploy a private console reachable over your peering or via a bastion/identity proxy. we support SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning and fine-grained RBAC.
[09:55] Omar: logging retention — can we set retention and ensure logs are purged per policy?
[09:59] Maya: yes, logs can be forwarded and you can set retention at your SIEM. we also support configurable retention in our console for audit logs.
[10:10] Jordan: wrap-up on technical asks — we'll send: network checklist, ip plan template, security whitepaper, pilot pricing, and a benchmark harness. what do you need from your side?
[10:21] Priya: we'll send VPC cidrs, a list of required regions, contacts for peering ops, and a sample traffic pattern for pilot. aim to provide by 2027-03-22.
[10:34] Alex: can we schedule a follow-up technical deep-dive with your infra team to validate transit gateway setup?
[10:39] Maya: yes, SE deep-dive next week works. we'll slot 60-90 minutes to go through route tables and a preliminary runbook.
[10:47] Jordan: Anything else?
[10:49] Lisa: one final thing — do you have any constraints on client IP ranges for rate limiting? we have internal egress proxies that NAT to limited addresses.
[10:58] Maya: we can accommodate static egress IPs; just include them in the ip plan.
[11:05] Alex: ok that covers most. thanks everyone.

End meeting transcript. 

Notes: occasional transcription errors present; product names and acronyms may be off in places (e.g., "privy").
next_steps: Redwood (Jordan/Maya) to send network checklist, IP planning template, security whitepaper, pilot pricing, and benchmark harness by 2027-03-17.
Vermillion (Priya/Alex) to share VPC CIDRs, list of allowed regions, peering ops contact, and sample traffic pattern by 2027-03-22.
Schedule SE-led deep-dive on transit gateway and route tables (60-90m) for week of 2027-03-22.

Maya Lin: Prepare benchmark harness and pilot runbook (due 2027-03-17).
